course_title: Combinatorial Theory: Introduction to Graph Theory, Extremal and Enumerative Combinatorics

term_conflict.handling: Preserve both descriptions; do not silently relabel the original files as Spring or assume a corrected academic term.

counting_policy: Expand explicitly labelled a,b,... into separate leaves, and count an unlettered top-level item as one leaf. Do not count unlettered multiple requests as extra printed leaves. HW4 Q3 points to two external exercises but is one printed numbered leaf; its alternative69 count is reported separately. External parts not present on these PDFs are not invented or counted as known subquestions. HW8 Q4 has two unlettered connectedness obligations within one printed leaf; both must be answered if selected.

category_definitions.external_statement_missing: Only external author/book/page/exercise number is public here; the full external statement has not been obtained under a compatible permission and must not be guessed.

exceptions_and_proof_workload.original_reading: random graph on n vertices with exactly 2n edges
exceptions_and_proof_workload.required_clarification: Use the uniform distribution over all simple labelled graphs with exactly 2n edges; n≥5 is necessary for that sample space to be nonempty.

exceptions_and_proof_workload.original_reading: Every two claw coverings of Γ−Δ are connected by reversing directed cycles, or directed 3-cycles.
exceptions_and_proof_workload.reason: Directed cycle reversal preserves every vertex outdegree. General claw coverings only force each outdegree to be a multiple of three and do not fix the outdegree vector. Two explicit coverings of the same icosahedral graph after deleting outer-face edges have different outdegree vectors.
exceptions_and_proof_workload.required_clarification: Retain the original assertion and the counterexample. A revised version may require the same outdegree vector; the intended standard 3-orientations additionally have outer vertices outdegree0 and every inner vertex outdegree3. Do not silently replace the printed general definition.

exceptions_and_proof_workload.reason: For n=1 these conditions give [0,∞), so P1 is not a bounded polytope and its volume is infinite. For n≥2 the adjacent constraints imply every x_i≤1.
exceptions_and_proof_workload.required_clarification: State n≥2 for the original region, or separately add 0≤x1≤1 when n=1 and label this as an editor correction.

exceptions_and_proof_workload.original_reading: Try to classify all finite connected planar vertex-transitive graphs; if not all, explain clearly the subclass classified.
exceptions_and_proof_workload.required_clarification: A complete classification of a clearly specified subclass is explicitly allowed by the official prompt. Examples alone do not establish a subclass classification. This inventory does not assert that the general classification is presently an open problem.

exceptions_and_proof_workload.original_reading: Every plane triangulation without separating triangles contains a Hamiltonian cycle.
exceptions_and_proof_workload.required_clarification: A full solution must prove the relevant Whitney theorem or a sufficient disk-triangulation lemma, with simple finite triangulation conventions and small cases addressed. Merely quoting the book’s previously external theorem is not a complete new official-homework solution.
exceptions_and_proof_workload.workload_note: Substantial independent topology/combinatorics proof; prioritize before promising all selected graph tasks are solved.

exceptions_and_proof_workload.original_reading: ω^(-1)σ is a cycle in Sn.
exceptions_and_proof_workload.required_clarification: One nontrivial cycle of length≥2, with all remaining points fixed; the identity does not describe an edge.

exceptions_and_proof_workload.original_reading: The graph of Pn has diameter two.
exceptions_and_proof_workload.reason: n=1 gives one vertex and diameter0; n=2 gives K2 and diameter1; n=3 gives K6 since every nonidentity permutation in S3 is one nontrivial cycle, so diameter1. For n≥4, disjoint transpositions supply a nonedge; the expected statement is diameter2.
exceptions_and_proof_workload.required_clarification: Separate n=1,2,3 and prove diameter exactly2 only for n≥4.

exceptions_and_proof_workload.reason: In simple undirected graph convention the n=1 and n=2 skeletons have respectively one and two vertices, hence no cycle.
exceptions_and_proof_workload.required_clarification: State n≥3 for a Hamiltonian cycle, and record the two exceptional skeletons.

exceptions_and_proof_workload.original_reading: c_n(H_n)=θ(log n), where H_n is a graph of an n-dim. hypercube. Both θ(log n) and “n-dim.” are visibly printed on the original PDF; the subscript on c_n is otherwise undefined.
exceptions_and_proof_workload.counterargument: Write Q_n for the n-dimensional cube. It has N=2^n vertices and m=n2^(n−1) edges. Each book page is an outerplanar graph on the same N spine vertices and has at most2N−3 edges. Thus c(Q_n)≥n2^(n−1)/(2^(n+1)−3)>n/4, ruling out Θ(log n).
exceptions_and_proof_workload.repair_and_upper_bound: Correct dimension-parametrized order is Θ(n). An explicit upper bound c(Q_n)≤n follows recursively: put two copies of a Q_(n−1) spine order consecutively in opposite orders, reuse the prior pages within the two disjoint blocks, and draw the corresponding-vertex matching on one new page; those matching intervals are nested and do not cross. If one instead denotes vertex count by N=2^n, the same order is Θ(log N). The original graph dimension cannot silently be changed to its vertex count.
exceptions_and_proof_workload.required_clarification: Retain the original formula, give the lower-bound refutation, then label the Θ(n) version as the editor’s repair.

exceptions_and_proof_workload.original_reading: All planar graphs have c(G)≤1000; hint invokes Hamiltonian graphs and Whitney.
exceptions_and_proof_workload.workload_note: Requires an actual bounded-page construction or its lemmas; proving the statement for already Hamiltonian planar graphs does not solve this subpart.

exceptions_and_proof_workload.original_reading: Permutations sortable with k queues and ℓ stacks have a finite forbidden-pattern basis, prove or disprove.
exceptions_and_proof_workload.scope: Outside the graph book’s main scope.
exceptions_and_proof_workload.required_clarification: If retained elsewhere, specify machine arrangement, ordering and allowed operations from course context. This inventory has not established current open/closed status and does not label it a proven contemporary open problem.

exceptions_and_proof_workload.original_reading: The locally defined α(G) is edge density m/binom(|V|,2), not independence number. Subpart(b) visibly reads α(G)≠1/3.
exceptions_and_proof_workload.required_clarification: Use a fresh density symbol such as ρ in the Chinese solution, declare the original local α convention, and require at least2 vertices for the finite density denominator.

exceptions_and_proof_workload.workload_note: A complete density-spectrum solution can use, but then must establish or explicitly define the accepted proof boundary of, an Erdős–Stone type complete-multipartite blow-up theorem. A bare assertion that infinite density is rational leaves the central implication unproved.

exceptions_and_proof_workload.original_reading: β(v) counts v′ with S(v)⊂S(v′), while β(R)=n and β(leaf)=1; label inequalities use the same printed subset symbol.
exceptions_and_proof_workload.required_clarification: Define β(v) as descendant-subtree size including v itself, as forced by the examples; require γ(v)<γ(v′) only for distinct vertices with v a proper ancestor of v′. Otherwise a non-strict reading would require γ(v)<γ(v).

hw2_claw_flip_counterexample.graph: icosahedral graph, with outer-face edges removed, not outer-face vertices
hw2_claw_flip_counterexample.vertex_construction: N=0, S=11; upper pentagon a_i=1+i, lower pentagon b_i=6+i, indices mod5. Full icosahedron edges are N-a_i, S-b_i, a_i-a_(i+1), b_i-b_(i+1), a_i-b_i, a_i-b_(i−1). Choose outer triangular face N,a0,a1.
hw2_claw_flip_counterexample.proof: Each displayed nonempty group consists of exactly three distinct edges with a common root, and the groups partition all27 remaining edges. Orient each group from its root. Reversing a directed cycle reverses one incoming and one outgoing edge at each cycle vertex, preserving every outdegree. Cover A has vertex2 outdegree0 and vertex7 outdegree3; cover B has these degrees reversed. Hence no sequence of directed cycle flips connects them; restricting to3-cycles cannot help.
hw2_claw_flip_counterexample.verification: Pure Python exact bipartite matching assigns every edge to a root slot; all displayed partitions and root-incidences rechecked by assertions. This is a finite counterexample, not a general classification.

It is not an audit of still-unwritten Chinese solutions, a final book PDF visual review, a ZIP clean rebuild, or remote publication verification.
